title: Bain Capital to Acquire Vitabiotics, the UK’s No.1 Vitamin Company
summary: Bain Capital to Acquire Vitabiotics, the UK’s No.1 Vitamin Company
body_text: Planned international expansion for one of the world’s leading independent vitamin, mineral and supplement businesses, with a presence in over 70 countries London - July 24, 2026 - 2026 : Bain Capital, a leading global private investment firm, today announced that it has agreed to acquire Vitabiotics, the UK’s No.1 Vitamin Company*, including its UK operations and the wider VB Group** (including Meyer Organics in India, and its operations in Africa, including VB Egypt), marking a significant milestone in Vitabiotics’ 55-year history and signalling the next phase of planned rapid international growth and expansion. The transaction brings together one of the world's leading healthcare and consumer investors with one of the most recognised independent vitamins, minerals and supplements businesses globally, creating a platform for accelerated international growth. The UK will remain central to Vitabiotics’ brand, innovation, and category leadership. There will be no immediate changes to day-to-day operations, and the company will continue to focus on delivering for customers, partners and consumers, while investing in areas including digital capabilities, e-commerce, international distribution, supply chain resilience and new product development. Given Vitabiotics’ global footprint, the investment will be led by Bain Capital’s Asia Private Equity team and supported by the firm’s global platform. Bain Capital will bring local market knowledge in India, together with sector expertise, portfolio resources and global capabilities, to support Vitabiotics as it continues to scale its brands, strengthen its international platform and invest in long-term growth within key markets such as MENA and China. Vitabiotics was founded in 1971 by visionary scientist and entrepreneur, Professor Kartar Lalvani OBE, who pioneered the nutraceutical field and innovative science-based formulas, leading to whole new categories of supplements and sector-leading brands supporting specific health and life-stage needs, resulting in a unique portfolio of sector-leading products, including several household names. Over the last decade under the leadership of his son, Tej Lalvani, Group Chief Executive Officer, the business has significantly accelerated its growth and leadership through product launches and partnerships. Having dedicated more than 30 years to working in the business, Tej Lalvani has played a central role in transforming Vitabiotics into one of the world's leading independent science-led nutraceutical companies. Outside Vitabiotics, he is widely recognised as one of the UK's leading entrepreneurs and as a Dragon on BBC TV’s Dragons' Den. As founder of the Group and in recognition of his life-time contribution and leadership in the supplement sector, Professor Kartar Lalvani will assume the honorary role of Chairman Emeritus on completion of the transaction. Professor Kartar Lalvani’s elder son, Professor Ajit Lalvani, has contributed his medical and scientific expertise to the business as non-executive director over three decades, alongside his distinguished clinical academic career. The Vitabiotics Group has built leading positions across several of the world's most attractive VMS markets, including India, China, Egypt and the wider MENA region, supported by a unique combination of consumer trust, healthcare professional credibility and local market expertise. As the UK’s leading vitamin company, its portfolio of trusted brands includes Pregnacare, Perfectil, Wellman, Wellwoman, Osteocare, and the Ultra range, supported by strong consumer trust, healthcare professional credibility and a growing international presence. Tej Lalvani, Group Chief Executive Officer of Vitabiotics, said: “This marks a defining moment in Vitabiotics’ journey. I'm incredibly grateful to have had the opportunity to build on my father's vision to harness the power of science and nutrition to improve everyday health and, together with our exceptional team, help transform Vitabiotics from a British family business into one of the world's most trusted vitamin and wellness companies. This direction is not about changing who we are; it is about accelerating what we can become. With Bain Capital’s global expertise and investment behind us, we have a unique opportunity to expand internationally, accelerate our innovation and take our trusted brands to millions more consumers, while staying true to the science, quality and values that have defined Vitabiotics for more than 55 years." Pawan Singh , a Partner at Bain Capital, said: “Vitabiotics is exactly the type of business we support: a trusted, science-led brand platform with category leadership, strong healthcare professional credibility and meaningful presence across the UK, India, the Middle East, Africa and China. Our India team has deep experience partnering with healthcare and consumer businesses, and we look forward to supporting Vitabiotics’ next phase of growth.” Rishi Mandawat , a Partner at Bain Capital added: “We see a compelling opportunity to help Vitabiotics build on its UK leadership and strengthen its global platform. Across Bain Capital, we will bring sector expertise, portfolio resources and local market knowledge to support investment in innovation, e-commerce, international distribution and operational capability.” Completion of the transaction remains subject to applicable closing conditgions, including customary regulatory approvals. Houlihan Lokey acted as exclusive corporate finance advisor to the selling party, advising on all aspects of the preparation, structuring, and negotiation of the transaction. Macfarlanes acted as lead legal adviser to the selling party, advising on all legal aspects of the sale and coordinating a large cross-border team. Rothschild & Co. acted as exclusive corporate finance adviser to Bain Capital. Kirkland & Ellis acted as lead legal adviser to Bain Capital, and Khaitan & co. acte4d as co-counsel advising Bain Capital on Indian law aspects of the transaction. ENDS About Bain Capital Founded in 1984, Bain Capital is one of the world’s leading private investment firms. We are committed to creating lasting impact for our investors, portfolio companies, and the communities in which we live. As a private partnership, we lead with conviction and a culture of collaboration, advantages that enable us to innovate investment approaches, unlock opportunities, and create exceptional outcomes. Our global platform invests across five focus areas: Private Equity, Growth & Venture, Capital Solutions, Credit & Capital Markets, and Real Assets. In these focus areas, we bring deep sector expertise and wide-ranging capabilities. We have 24 offices on four continents, more than 1,900 employees, and approximately $225 billion in assets under management. To learn more, visit www.baincapital.com . Follow @BainCapital on LinkedIn and X (Twitter). About Vitabiotics Vitabiotics’ mission is to empower wellness and healthy living through innovation in nutritional healthcare. The company has pioneered advances in nutritional healthcare for 55 years, with a portfolio that includes some of Britain’s leading and most trusted supplement brands such as Perfectil, Pregnacare, Wellman, Wellwoman and Menopace. Vitabiotics is the leading British nutraceutical company founded in 1971 by Professor Kartar Lalvani, with a heritage deeply rooted in family entrepreneurship and scientific research. Built on a foundation of clinical insight into nutritional science, the company developed some of the UK’s most trusted supplement brands, including Perfectil, Pregnacare, Wellman, Wellwoman, and Menopace. It has grown into a category-defining business in vitamins and mineral-based food supplements, with products spanning key health areas and life stages, including pregnancy, men’s and women’s health, beauty, and family nutrition. In 2013, Vitabiotics became the UK’s largest vitamin company by sales value, reflecting its strong market position and sustained consumer trust. As the UK’s No.1 vitamin company *, Vitabiotics UK exports to over 70 countries worldwide. Alongside its international export business, the Group has established operations in key global markets including India, China, Egypt and West Africa, reflecting its evolution into a leading international nutritional healthcare company. Vitabiotics is the only vitamin company to have received the Queen’s Award for Enterprise on four occasions, including twice for Innovation (in 2013 for Pregnacare and in 2018 for Perfectil). Vitabiotics also supports ongoing research and original clinical trials in collaboration with universities and leading medical centres in the UK and internationally. About Professor Kartar Lalvani OBE Professor Kartar Lalvani’s Doctorate of Science in Medicinal Chemistry (University of Bonn) underpinned his mission to transform preventive healthcare through scientifically formulated vitamins and minerals. At a time when supplementation was often dismissed as unnecessary, he founded Vitabiotics, UK (1971) and Meyer Organics, India (1982) to combine research-led innovation, pharmaceutical-grade quality manufacturing and clinical validation. He appointed his former mentor from King’s College London, the renowned Professor Arnold Beckett OBE, as Vitabiotics’ first Chairman (see picture). Professor Lalvani’s entrepreneurial talent drove innovation across the whole product development process, from patented formulations to unique brand names, product design and marketing. Now in his 95th year, his many accolades include Ernst & Young Master Entrepreneur of the Year (2008), Honorary Professorship of the University of Franche-Comte, France (2014), and the Lifetime Achievement Award of the Federation of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of India (2025), as well as Vitabiotics’ winning the Queen’s Award for Enterprise on four occasions. Having pioneered the new paradigm of nutraceutical therapy, Professor Lalvani poignantly observes that “while the last century was the century of antibiotics, this is the century of vitamins”. About Professor Tej Lalvani Tej Lalvani has served as Chief Executive Officer of Vitabiotics for the last decade, having worked within the family business for more than 30 years, including previously as Chief Operating Officer. Under his leadership, Vitabiotics has rapidly scaled its position as the leading VMS player in the UK and on a global scale. Outside of Vitabiotics, Tej Lalvani is widely recognised as an entrepreneur and investor, having appeared for five seasons as a Dragon on BBC’s Dragons’ Den. He has received multiple business and entrepreneurship awards, holds an Honorary Doctorate and Visiting Professorship for entrepreneurship and business from the University of Westminster, and was recently inducted into the Great British Entrepreneur Awards Hall of Fame. Notes to Editors: *Nielsen GB ScanTrack Value and Unit Sales 52 w/e 4th October 2025 **Certain group entities operating in jurisdictions outside the scope of this transaction will continue to trade under the existing beneficial ownership structure and are not part of the acquisition.

title: Hotel Room Block vs Airbnb for Wedding Guests: Which Is Better?
summary: For most weddings, a hotel room block is the better choice. It simplifies transportation, keeps guests together, and hotels may offer discounted group
body_text: Last Updated on July 23, 2026 by Joy Editors For most weddings, a hotel room block is the better choice. It simplifies transportation, keeps guests together, and hotels may offer discounted group rates compared with standard pricing, although savings vary by property, season, and destination. Airbnb works better for small destination weddings, rural venues with few hotels nearby, or when a group of guests wants to share a house. Many couples offer both options. One of the most common accommodation questions couples face is whether to set up a hotel room block , suggest Airbnb, or both. The answer depends on your guest count, venue location, transportation plan, and what kind of experience you want guests to have. Here is a full comparison to help you decide. Side-by-Side Comparison Factor Hotel Room Block Airbnb Cost per guest Hotels may offer discounted group rates; savings vary by property and season Varies widely; cheaper per person when shared Transportation Easy: one shuttle pickup point Complex: multiple scattered locations Guest experience Guests stay together, easy to socialize Separate, more private Accessibility ADA-compliant rooms available Varies by property, often limited Couple’s financial risk Attrition risk on contracted blocks None Booking simplicity for guests One link, standard process Guests book independently Availability in rural areas Limited or none Often more options Group bonding High: shared lobby, hotel bar, morning brunch Low: guests spread across different properties When a Hotel Room Block Is the Better Choice A hotel room block works best when: You have 20 or more out-of-town guests who need accommodation You are planning shuttle transportation between the hotel and venue You want guests to socialize before and after the wedding (hotel lobby, bar, morning brunch) Some guests need ADA-accessible rooms Your venue is in a city or suburban area with multiple hotel options You want a consistent, predictable experience for all guests Best for City and suburban weddings, weddings with 50+ guests, any event where you are providing shuttle transportation, and couples who want guests to experience the full wedding weekend together. When Airbnb Is the Better Choice Airbnb makes more sense when: Your venue is in a rural area with few or no hotels nearby You have a small guest list (under 30 guests) who know each other well A group of guests wants to share a large house for a multi-day celebration Your wedding has a retreat or house-party feel where guests staying together is part of the experience You are hosting a destination wedding in a location with limited hotel inventory Best for Intimate destination weddings, rural venues, elopements with a small guest group, and situations where the accommodation is part of the celebration itself. The Transportation Problem with Airbnb The biggest practical challenge with Airbnb for wedding guests is transportation . When guests are scattered across multiple properties, you cannot run a single shuttle route. Either guests arrange their own rides (which means some will be late or need to leave early to avoid driving after drinking), or you need multiple pickup points, which adds significant cost and complexity. With a hotel room block, all guests staying at the block hotel can board one shuttle. The logistics are simple, the cost is predictable, and no one has to worry about driving after the reception. Pro tip: If you are considering Airbnb for some guests, still set up a hotel room block for guests who need transportation or accessible accommodations. List both options on your wedding website and let guests choose. Cost Comparison: Hotel Block vs Airbnb The cost comparison depends heavily on location and group size. Hotels may offer discounted group rates compared with standard pricing, although savings vary by property, season, and destination. Here are two common scenarios: Scenario 1: City Wedding (25 out-of-town guests) Option Estimated Cost per Room/Night Notes Hotel room block (group rate) $150-$200 Discounted group rate; savings vary by hotel and season Airbnb (private room) $120-$180 Varies widely; cleaning fees add $30-$80 per stay Airbnb (shared house, 8 guests) $60-$90 per person Cheaper per person but not all guests want to share Scenario 2: Rural Destination Wedding (20 out-of-town guests) Option Estimated Cost Notes Nearest hotel (30 min away) $120-$160/room/night No group rate likely; small hotel or motel Airbnb (large house, 10-12 guests) $50-$80 per person/night Better value; guests share common spaces In rural settings, Airbnb often wins on cost and convenience because hotel options are limited or far from the venue. In cities, hotel room blocks are usually the better value once group rates are applied. What About Offering Both? Many couples set up a hotel room block and also mention Airbnb as an alternative on their wedding website. This works well when: You have a mix of guests: families who want space, couples who prefer a hotel, and individuals who want the cheapest option Your hotel block fills up and you need an overflow option Some guests specifically prefer Airbnb and would rather not stay at a hotel On your wedding website , list the hotel block with the booking link and deadline, then add a note that Airbnb options are also available in the area for guests who prefer them. This gives everyone a clear path without forcing a single option. A wedding website is the simplest way to share all accommodation details in one place. Couples can add hotel room block details with booking deadlines, Airbnb suggestions for guests who prefer them, shuttle information and transportation logistics , and an online RSVP so guests can confirm attendance and accommodation preferences at the same time. For destination weddings, this guide walks through setting up travel details step by step. Accessibility: A Reason to Always Offer a Hotel Option Airbnb properties vary widely in accessibility. Most are not ADA-compliant, and many have stairs, narrow doorways, or other barriers that make them difficult or impossible for guests with mobility limitations. Hotels are required to offer ADA-accessible rooms, and a hotel room block ensures those rooms are available at the group rate. Even if most of your guests would be fine with Airbnb, setting up a hotel block ensures that every guest has a comfortable option. The Social Case for Hotel Blocks One underrated benefit of hotel room blocks is what happens outside the ceremony and reception. When guests stay at the same hotel, they run into each other in the lobby, share rides to the venue, grab breakfast together the morning after, and extend the celebration in ways that are harder to replicate when everyone is scattered across different Airbnbs. For couples who want the wedding weekend to feel like a full experience rather than a single event, a hotel block creates the conditions for that to happen naturally. Frequently Asked Questions Should I do a hotel room block or let guests book Airbnb? For most weddings, a hotel room block is the better choice because it simplifies transportation, keeps guests together, and hotels may offer discounted group rates. Airbnb works better for small destination weddings where guests want a shared house experience or when the venue is in a rural area with few hotels. Is Airbnb cheaper than a hotel room block for wedding guests? It depends on the location and group size. Airbnb can be cheaper per person when guests share a large house, but hotel room blocks may offer discounted group rates compared with standard pricing. In cities, hotel blocks are frequently a better value per room than comparable Airbnb options, especially for single or double occupancy. Savings vary by property, season, and destination. Can I offer both a hotel room block and Airbnb options to guests? Yes, and many couples do. A hotel room block covers guests who prefer a hotel experience or need accessible accommodations, while Airbnb works for families or groups who want to share a house. List both options on your wedding website so guests can choose. What happens if guests do not fill the hotel room block? If you have a courtesy block, unused rooms are released at the cutoff date and you owe nothing. If you have a contracted block with an attrition clause, you may owe the hotel for unfilled rooms above the threshold. This is why courtesy blocks are recommended for most couples.

title: Auth0 Open Source (2026): What's Free and What Are The Top OSS Alternatives
summary: Is Auth0 open source? What's actually OSS, and which open-source Auth0 alternatives (Keycloak, Ory, SuperTokens) fit your stack in 2026?
body_text: When you’re choosing an authentication platform, open source can be a dealbreaker. Maybe you need full control over your authentication infrastructure. Maybe you want to avoid vendor lock-in. Or maybe you just want to see exactly how your authentication works under the hood. Auth0 comes up in almost every discussion of authentication. But is it actually open source? And if not, what are your best alternatives? Let’s clear this up. TL;DR: Is Auth0 Open Source? Short answer: No, Auth0 is not open source. Auth0 is a proprietary SaaS platform. You can’t self-host it. You can’t see the source code for the core platform. You’re entirely dependent on Auth0’s infrastructure and pricing. That said, Auth0 does release some open-source projects. They maintain client SDKs and a few standalone tools under open-source licenses. But the authentication platform itself? That’s closed source. This matters because if you need an open-source authentication system, you can’t just grab Auth0 and run it yourself. You need a different solution. What Auth0 Actually Open-Sources Auth0 contributes to open source, but not where it counts most. Here’s what they actually release publicly. SDKs and Client Libraries Auth0 publishes client libraries under open-source licenses (usually MIT). These help you integrate with their hosted service. What’s available: JavaScript SDKs for React, Angular, Vue Mobile SDKs for iOS and Android Backend SDKs for Node.js, Python, Java, Go Auth0 CLI for managing configurations Sample apps and quickstart templates These are helpful for developers using Auth0. You can read the code, submit pull requests, and understand how the integration works. But they only work with Auth0’s proprietary backend. You can’t use these SDKs to build your own authentication system. OpenFGA (Fine-Grained Authorization) This is Auth0’s most substantial open-source contribution. OpenFGA is a fully open-source authorization system inspired by Google’s Zanzibar. What it does: Manages complex permissions and relationships Handles questions like “Can user X edit document Y?” Scales to millions of permission checks Runs completely independently from Auth0 Important distinction: OpenFGA handles authorization (who can do what), not authentication (who you are). It doesn’t manage users, passwords, or login flows. You still need an authentication system alongside it. You can self-host OpenFGA for free, or use Auth0’s managed version. Either way, it’s separate from authentication. What Stays Proprietary Everything that makes Auth0 actually work is closed source: User database and management Login flows and session handling Password storage and verification Multi-factor authentication Social login integrations The admin dashboard All the infrastructure and scaling logic You can’t self-host any of this. You can’t modify it. You can’t see how it works. You’re completely dependent on Auth0’s service. If You Need an Open-Source Platform for Authentication: Leading Options If you actually need open-source authentication (not just open-source SDKs), you’ve got three solid choices in 2026. SuperTokens: Modern OSS with a Managed Option SuperTokens gives you full open-source authentication that you can self-host for free. They also offer managed hosting if you want it. Why it works: The entire authentication core is Apache 2.0 licensed. That means you get complete source code access. You can self-host it. You can modify it. You own your authentication infrastructure. Unlike Auth0’s SDK-only approach, SuperTokens open-sources the actual authentication platform. User management, sessions, login flows — everything. How it’s different from Auth0: SuperTokens keeps your JWT verification keys on your domain. Your application verifies tokens locally without calling back to SuperTokens servers. This means: Faster authentication (no network round-trips) Better reliability (works even if SuperTokens go down) Easy migration (standard JWT tokens work anywhere) No vendor lock-in (you’re not tied to proprietary formats) Auth0 requires your app to call their servers for token verification. That creates dependency and latency. Developer experience: SuperTokens focuses on giving developers control. You can override any authentication endpoint. You can customize flows without hitting platform limitations. You can embed authentication directly in your app instead of redirecting to hosted pages. The code is readable and well-documented. When something breaks, you can actually debug it yourself. When to choose SuperTokens: You want open-source control, with a modern developer experience. You might start self-hosted, but move to managed later (or vice versa). You need deep customization without rebuilding everything. You want to avoid vendor lock-in from day one. For more details, check out the SuperTokens vsAuth0 comparison. Keycloak: Enterprise OSS with Everything Included Keycloak is the veteran of open-source authentication. It’s been around since 2014, is backed by Red Hat, and handles enterprise requirements out of the box. What you get: Full identity and access management SAML, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect support User federation and LDAP integration Fine-grained authorization Comprehensive admin console When to choose Keycloak: You need enterprise features like SAML and identity brokering. You’re already in the Red Hat / Java ecosystem. You want a mature, battle-tested solution. You have the ops capacity to run Java infrastructure. Trade-offs: Keycloak is powerful, but heavyweight. It’s Java-based, which means higher resource usage. The learning curve is steeper. Setup and configuration take more time than lighter alternatives. Ory: Modular OSS Components Ory takes a different approach. Instead of one monolithic platform, they offer separate components you compose together. The components: Ory Kratos (user management and authentication) Ory Hydra (OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect server) Ory Oathkeeper (identity and access proxy) Ory Keto (permissions and authorization) When to choose Ory: You want to pick exactly which pieces you need. You’re comfortable with microservices architecture. You need OAuth 2.0 or OIDC server capabilities. You like having control over each component. Trade-offs: The modular approach gives you flexibility but adds complexity. You need to understand how the pieces fit together. You’re managing multiple services instead of one unified platform. Ory also offers managed hosting (Ory Network) if you don’t want to run it yourself. Decision Pillars: When to Go OSS vs Hosted Choosing between open source and hosted platforms isn’t just about philosophy. There are real trade-offs. Hosting and Control Open source (SuperTokens, Keycloak, Ory): Full control over infrastructure Self-host in your VPC or on-premises Complete data ownership You handle scaling and uptime Hosted (Auth0): No infrastructure to manage Auth0 handles scaling and security Multi-tenant shared infrastructure Less control over data and deployment If you need data to stay in specific regions, require air-gapped deployments, or have strict compliance requirements, open source gives you options hosted platforms can’t match. Developer Experience and Speed Hosted platforms ship faster initially: Pre-built UI components Managed social login integrations Less infrastructure setup Support team available Open source requires more setup: You deploy and configure everything You handle updates and security patches You build integrations yourself (or use what’s available) Community support instead of dedicated help If you’re racing to launch and don’t have devops capacity, hosted makes sense. If you have engineers who can handle infrastructure, open source gives you more long-term flexibility. Cost Model Open source costs: $0 in licensing fees Infrastructure costs (servers, database, bandwidth) Engineering time for deployment and maintenance Potential support contracts if you want them Hosted platform costs: Usually per monthly active user (MAU) Add-ons for features like MFA or SSO Pricing scales automatically with usage No infrastructure management overhead For small projects, hosted can be cheaper (free tiers are generous). As you scale to 100K+ users, open source often becomes more cost-effective despite operational overhead. Quick Best-Fit Snapshots Not sure which option fits your needs? Here are some quick recommendations. Need open source with enterprise features? → Keycloak Best for organizations that need SAML support, identity provider brokering, user federation, and comprehensive enterprise capabilities. Worth the operational complexity if you need the features. Need open source with fast integration? → SuperTokens Best for teams that want a modern developer experience, clean APIs, and the option to switch between self-hosted and managed hosting. Good balance of control and convenience. Need modular components you can compose? → Ory Best for teams comfortable with microservices who want to pick exactly which authentication pieces they need. Offers maximum flexibility at the cost of complexity. Need hosted simplicity and don’t care about open source? → Auth0 Best for teams prioritizing speed over control, with budget for per-user pricing as you scale. Good if you want everything managed for you. For a broader comparison of Auth0 alternatives, see the top Auth0 alternatives in 2025 guide. Conclusion Auth0 isn’t open source. The platform itself is proprietary, even though they release some SDKs and tools under open-source licenses. If you actually need open-source authentication, you’re looking at Keycloak, Ory, or SuperTokens. Each has different strengths: Keycloak for enterprise breadth and maturity. Ory for modular, composable architecture. SuperTokens for modern DX with managed optionality. The choice depends on what you value more: control or convenience, upfront speed or long-term flexibility, infrastructure costs, or engineering time. Before committing, run a time-boxed pilot. Deploy your top choice in staging. Build a sample integration. See how it feels to work with. Authentication is too important to choose based on blog posts alone. For teams wanting open-source control without rebuilding authentication from scratch, SuperTokens offers a pragmatic middle ground. Full source code access, modern developer experience, and the flexibility to self-host or use managed hosting as your needs change.

title: How does a uniform rental program work?
summary: Learn how a uniform rental program works, from sizing and delivery to upkeep. See how businesses improve consistency, control costs, and maintain workwear.
body_text: A managed uniform rental program takes the complexity out of managing your team’s workwear. It begins with garment sizing and selection customized to your brand and safety needs. Once established, the program runs on a dependable weekly cycle: a provider picks up soiled uniforms, professionally launders and inspects them for repairs, and returns clean garments directly to your facility. With ongoing support handling inventory adjustments and employee changes, it’s a hands-off, cost-effective solution for busy operations. Read on to explore how the rental cycle works and get answers to frequently asked questions. Table of Contents A uniform rental program explainer for businesses Managing employee workwear on your own can drain your valuable time and capital. Procurement managers and operations directors frequently deal with the administrative burden of tracking inventory, replacing damaged clothing, and ensuring safety compliance. Purchasing garments directly or trying to manage a work uniform rental process internally can require a large initial investment and leave ongoing maintenance responsibilities squarely on your team, making an outsourced uniform rental service far more valuable. Outsourcing this process helps eliminate common operational bottlenecks. By centralizing procurement through a uniform rental program, businesses gain a more efficient uniform rental service that supports cost control , simplifies workwear management, and ensures employees always have access to clean, professional work uniforms. What happens during the initial setup and garment assignment? The uniform rental process begins with an assessment of your business’s safety requirements, job functions, and branding needs. Employees are then measured to ensure a proper, comfortable fit and assigned the appropriate garments for their roles. how a UniFirst uniform rental program works Each employee receives 11 uniforms 5 uniforms clean and ready to wear during the workweek 5 uniforms being washed and processed at the facility 1 uniform being worn on the scheduled service day How uniform rental service pickup, laundering, and delivery works Consistency is what makes a uniform rental program run smoothly. At the end of each shift, employees place soiled garments in a designated collection bin or return area. On your scheduled service day, your Route Service Representative (RSR) collects the soiled garments from your facility and takes them back to our laundry facilities to be professionally laundered and inspected. Fresh, clean uniforms are then returned as part of the regular delivery cycle, ensuring employees always have the garments they need for work. The 3-step unifirst uniform rental cycle Step 1 Pickup The RSR collects the soiled uniforms from the designated return area and transports them to our laundry facility. Step 2 Process Uniforms undergo industrial-grade laundering and inspected by an automated system to identify any required repairs. Step 3 Deliver Freshly cleaned uniforms are returned to employee lockers, maintaining a seamless uniform rotation. How ongoing repairs and size changes are managed Reputable uniform providers utilize advanced tracking to manage garment lifecycles. UniFirst uses an Automatic Mend System that includes a 10-point inspection during the processing phase. This system catches 97% of necessary repairs before the customer even reports an issue. If an employee changes sizes or leaves the company, the uniform rental program automatically adjusts the inventory, eliminating excess stock and unnecessary costs. What are the main business benefits of a uniform rental program? If minimizing upfront capital expenditure matters more than purchasing directly and owning your own inventory, uniform rental makes the most sense. In terms of cost, here’s what you can expect: Uniform rental prices vary by garment type, employee count, pickup frequency, and service needs. Industry pricing data shows that businesses typically spend $4 to $15 per wearer per week. These uniform rental prices usually cover the garments, laundering, delivery, and automatic replacements, giving your business a predictable cost structure and helping protect your budget from surprise expenses. How professional uniforms help improve employee safety and brand image Standardized, high-quality work uniforms ensure consistency across all locations. A unified appearance boosts your brand image and fosters customer trust. Furthermore, renting specialized safety workwear, like CAT 1–4 flame-resistant clothing , or hi-vis shirts , helps ensure your team remains protected against potential workplace hazards, while ensuring compliance with OSHA, NFPA, and ANSI standards. How industrial laundering ensures hygiene and safety compliance Home washing machines simply cannot deliver the sanitation levels required in compliance-heavy industries like food processing, manufacturing, or healthcare. When employees wash their uniforms at home , there is no way to guarantee critical controls like precise water temperatures or specialized wash formulas necessary to eliminate foodborne pathogens and cross-contamination risks. To help mitigate these risks, UniFirst operates over 81 facilities with TRSA Hygienically Clean Food Safety certification, helping to ensure that garments are processed under strict standards. Our proprietary laundering processes are designed to support your facility’s HACCP (Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point) plans and align with GFSI (Global Food Safety Initiative) recognized standards. By partnering with a certified uniform rental provider such as UniFirst, operations managers can confidently maintain compliant workwear that stands up to rigorous third-party safety audits. Why outsourcing uniforms improves overall operational efficiency A uniform rental program removes the administrative hassle of daily workwear management. Your human resources and procurement teams no longer need to track down lost shirts, negotiate individual replacement orders, or manage laundry contracts. To maximize this efficiency, UniFirst offers customers 24/7 access to the UniFirst Portal . Instead of waiting on phone calls or back-and-forth emails, the digital portal puts complete control in your pocket at the touch of a button. Customers can instantly log in to create service requests, track garment deliveries, or add and delete wearers in real time. By combining automated routing with immediate digital account management, a uniform rental program transforms a tedious operational chore into a streamlined, hands-off process. Why choose UniFirst for your uniform rental program Choosing UniFirst means choosing a uniform program built entirely around your bottom line, your operational efficiency, and your peace of mind. We deliver a fully managed service model designed to maximize your return on investment while helping to keep your workforce safe, compliant, and professional on the job. Experience the UniFirst Difference Customized for savings and scale Minimize waste and control costs with a scalable program for your exact budget and workforce size, whether you have a single or multiple locations. UniFirst Portal Get more control with 24/7 access to the UniFirst Portal . View invoices, add/remove wearers, and request service from a single, frictionless dashboard. 90 years of service Partner with an industry leader that combines nearly a century of expertise with the trust of 300,000+ business locations and outfits more than 2 million workers every day. Streamline your uniform procurement today A managed uniform rental program can turn a time-consuming administrative task into a more predictable, cost-effective process. By working with a reputable uniform rental company, businesses can help protect employees, support a consistent brand image, and stay productive on daily operations. If you are evaluating options, requesting a cost analysis is a practical next step for comparing service levels, support, and overall fit. Frequently asked questions Frequently asked questions How much does uniform rental cost? Uniform rental cost typically ranges from $4 to $15 per wearer per week, but pricing depends on several factors, including garment type, employee count, pickup frequency, laundering requirements, repairs, customization, and service location. In most cases, these uniform rental prices cover garment supply, weekly delivery, industrial laundering, repairs, and size exchanges, giving businesses a reliable and predictable cost structure. How long does it take to implement a new uniform program? Implementation timelines vary by company size, but standard setups generally take a few weeks. This period includes employee sizing, garment customization, and establishing the weekly service schedule. What are the risks of buying instead of renting? Purchasing uniforms gives your business full ownership, but it also comes with higher upfront costs and more internal responsibility. When comparing uniform rental vs. purchase for businesses, buying may make sense if you do not need ongoing laundering or frequent replacements. However, your team must manage inventory, repairs, size changes, replacement orders, and garment distribution in-house. It also places cleaning responsibility on employees, which can create inconsistencies in appearance, hygiene, and safety compliance. By contrast, a uniform rental program offers more predictable service, professional laundering, repair support, and easier inventory control, making it a more reliable option for many businesses. What are the alternatives to a full uniform rental program? If weekly laundering is not required, businesses can choose a uniform lease program or a direct purchase program . Leasing spreads out the garment cost over time but leaves laundering to the employee, while direct purchase transfers complete ownership and maintenance responsibility to the buyer. Who benefits most from managed uniform rental services? Virtually any business can benefit from a managed uniform rental program by eliminating the administrative hassle and upfront costs of managing workwear. However, it is especially valuable for businesses that need: Strict hygiene and sanitation controls: Such as food processing, manufacturing, or healthcare facilities where home laundering cannot guarantee cross-contamination safety. Specialized safety and compliance apparel: such as oil and gas, utilities, or industrial operations that require certified flame-resistant (FR) or high-visibility garments to meet strict OSHA, NFPA, or ANSI standards. Enhanced brand consistency: Businesses with public-facing teams, multiple locations, or large field service workforces that rely on a clean, uniform brand image to build customer trust. Centralized procurement and budget control: Multi-facility organizations that need predictable, transparent weekly pricing and automated inventory management to eliminate waste and control total cost of ownership.

title: Cooper Standard Earns Golden Scale Award for FlexiCore™ Technology

summary: We spend a lot of time talking about why teams choose Superwall. But today, let's be honest about the situations where another tool — RevenueCat, Adapty, or just AI-assisted coding — is the better fit.
body_text: Superwall was built for teams who want to experiment fast, optimize paywalls deeply, and tie every decision to real revenue impact. It is a tool for people who see monetization as a product function, not just a payment screen. That said, there are great reasons to choose something else. Different products solve different problems, and if you are optimizing for something other than paywall performance, we can save you the trouble right now. Here are a few honest reasons you shouldn't use Superwall . 1. If you primarily need subscription management across web and mobile If your challenge is managing web subscriptions, verifying receipts, or syncing data across multiple platforms, RevenueCat is the stronger choice.
