title: How to Prepare for a State Survey at a Skilled Nursing Facility
summary: A practical state survey readiness playbook for skilled nursing facilities, covering the survey process, documentation, and equipment that surveyors check.
body_text: To prepare for a state survey at a skilled nursing facility, treat readiness as a year-round routine rather than a survey-week scramble. Keep your documentation current, run your care and safety systems the same way every day, and make sure every piece of equipment can be located, is maintained on schedule, and can be documented on the spot. Surveys are unannounced, so the only reliable state is always ready. This is the plain-language version, written for an administrator or director of nursing, not a compliance consultant. It walks the survey process as it actually works, the readiness habits that hold up under scrutiny, and one slice most buildings leave to chance: the equipment surveyors can physically touch. First, understand how the survey actually works You cannot prepare for something you picture wrong, so start with the mechanics. State surveys of skilled nursing facilities are conducted by state survey agencies on behalf of CMS under the federal survey and certification rules in 42 CFR Part 488 . Two facts shape everything about how you prepare. First, standard surveys are unannounced . Notifying a facility of the date, or causing it to be notified, is prohibited and carries a federal penalty. You will not get a warning, and any readiness plan that depends on advance notice is built on sand. Second, they are recurring on a rolling window . A facility must receive a standard survey no later than 15 months after the last day of its previous one, and the statewide average interval must be 12 months or less. So while the exact date is unknown, the rough cadence is not: plan to be ready roughly once a year, every year. Surveyors spend several days on site. They observe care, interview residents, families, and staff, review records, and inspect the physical environment and equipment. Findings that fall short of a requirement are cited as deficiencies, tagged with an "F-tag" that maps to a specific rule in 42 CFR Part 483 , the requirements for long-term care facilities. If you are new to the tag system, our SNF survey readiness checklist lays out the sequence step by step. Build a readiness routine, not a countdown Because the survey is unannounced, the winning strategy is boring on purpose: a light, repeatable monthly routine so that any given week you are already in survey shape. The building that scrambles when it senses a window is opening is the building that gets caught with a stale log or a device nobody can find. A workable monthly loop looks like this: Reconcile documentation. Confirm care plans, assessments, and required logs are current and match what is actually happening on the floor. A record that contradicts practice is worse than no record. Run your safety and maintenance checks. Preventive maintenance, equipment safety checks, and environmental rounds happen on schedule, and the schedule is documented. Confirm the physical environment. Walk the building the way a surveyor would. Hazards, clutter, and out-of-service equipment get fixed and logged, not stepped around. Close open items. Anything flagged last month is resolved or has a dated plan, so nothing rots into a pattern. The point is that readiness is a state you maintain, not a project you start. The scramble version of this, where a building tries to compress a year of upkeep into a frantic week, is exactly the failure mode we describe in the survey-week equipment scramble . The equipment slice: locate, maintain, document Most survey-prep guides stop at clinical documentation. But surveyors physically inspect the building, and equipment is one of the most tangible things they can examine and one of the easiest to be caught flat-footed on. Three things have to be true for every durable medical asset you own: you can locate it, it is maintained, and you can document both on demand. Locate You cannot show a surveyor an item you cannot find, and you cannot prove a resident has the assistive device their care plan calls for if the device has wandered to another wing. In a typical building, equipment moves all day: beds ride out on discharges, chairs travel to appointments, lifts migrate between rooms. A static inventory list is a photograph of a fleet that never holds still, accurate the day you finish it and wrong by Monday. Locating equipment on demand is the foundation of the other two. It is also where nurses quietly lose 30 to 60 minutes a shift hunting for things, time that comes straight out of resident care. A building that can pull up any item's current room in seconds is a building that walks a surveyor to the device instead of apologizing for it. Maintain Essential equipment must be kept in safe operating condition. That is not a soft expectation, it is the substance of F908, Essential Equipment, Safe Operating Condition , at 42 CFR 483.90(d)(2) , which requires facilities to "maintain all mechanical, electrical, and patient care equipment in safe operating condition." Preventive maintenance runs on the manufacturer's recommended schedule, repairs are tracked, and out-of-service items are tagged and pulled, not left in circulation. A visibly broken chair or an overdue lift is a finding waiting to happen. We go deeper on that tag in F908, essential equipment maintained . Document Locating and maintaining only count if you can prove them. When a surveyor asks for a specific lift's service history or the preventive maintenance record for your beds, the answer needs to be a document, not a promise to look. The buildings that fumble here are usually the ones keeping maintenance history in a binder that lives in one person's office, or worse, in that person's memory. Instant, itemized records are the difference between a clean line of questioning and a deficiency. Our guide to equipment documentation for a nursing home survey covers exactly what to keep and how. The equipment-adjacent tags worth knowing Equipment is rarely the whole story of a citation, but it is a recurring contributor across several tags. Knowing which ones touch equipment tells you where to concentrate. The one to know first is F689, Free of Accident Hazards, Supervision, and Devices , at 42 CFR 483.25(d) , which is consistently among the most frequently cited tags on standard surveys. It covers keeping the environment as free of accident hazards as possible and giving residents the supervision and assistive devices they need to prevent avoidable accidents. The clinical judgment and supervision inside that tag are a whole-building responsibility. But a missing or broken assistive device, or a hazard nobody flagged because nobody could see the equipment, is a concrete and preventable contributor. Equipment also brushes up against the tags for pressure-ulcer support surfaces, respiratory care equipment, and infection-control cleaning of shared devices. The regulatory substance of each lives in 42 CFR Part 483 , and the interpretive guidance surveyors use is in the CMS State Operations Manual Appendix PP, published at cms.gov . In every one of them, the clinical care is yours to run. The narrow, honest role of good equipment practice is to remove the equipment-shaped reasons a citation gets written. Where Norra fits, and where it does not Be clear-eyed about scope. No software makes a building survey-ready on its own, and readiness spans clinical care, infection control, staffing, and documentation that no vendor handles for you. Any product that claims to "guarantee compliance" or "prevent citations" is overselling, and surveyors are not fooled by it. Norra covers one specific slice, and covers it well: keeping durable medical equipment locatable, maintained, and instantly documentable. Proprietary smart tags go on every asset and plug-in gateways report each item's room continuously, with no wiring and no scanning, so the inventory keeps itself current instead of going stale. When a surveyor asks where an item is or when it was last serviced, the answer is on screen in seconds rather than in a binder down the hall. The same visibility that makes equipment survey-ready also removes waste the rest of the year. Buildings on Norra have reached zero unnecessary rentals, cut equipment spending by as much as 70 percent, placed 90 percent fewer new rental orders, and freed over 1,100 staff hours a year that used to go to hunting for equipment. The approach is proven across a multi-facility skilled nursing network, installs at a fraction of the cost of hospital-grade tracking, and Norra is Y Combinator-backed and a MatrixCare marketplace partner with a live integration that works alongside any EHR. Missing, unmaintained, or undocumented equipment is a common contributor to citations under several tags. Norra reduces that specific risk and makes the equipment paperwork instant. That is a modest, concrete claim, and it is the right one: keep the equipment part of survey readiness handled, so your team can spend its attention on the clinical care that no tool can do for you.

title: TeraWulf Announces Anthropic Lease at Justified Data Campus and Sale of Majority Interest in Abernathy Joint Venture to Fluidstack
summary: Long-Term AI Infrastructure Lease Expected to Generate ~$19 Billion of Contracted Revenue Over Initial Term Abernathy Transaction…...
body_text: TeraWulf Announces Anthropic Lease at Justified Data Campus and Sale of Majority Interest in Abernathy Joint Venture to Fluidstack July 06, 2026 8:00am EDT Long-Term AI Infrastructure Lease Expected to Generate ~$19 Billion of Contracted Revenue Over Initial Term Abernathy Transaction Monetizes Approximately $450 Million Investment at a Premium and Provides Capital to Expand Wholly Owned AI Infrastructure Portfolio EASTON, Md., July 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TeraWulf Inc. (Nasdaq: WULF) (“TeraWulf” or the “Company”), a leading owner, developer, and operator of vertically integrated digital infrastructure, today announced two significant transactions that further advance its strategy of developing, owning, and operating large-scale AI infrastructure campuses. The Company has executed a 20-year lease agreement with Anthropic at its Justified Data campus in Hawesville, Kentucky. The lease is expected to generate approximately $19 billion of contracted revenue over the initial lease term. Separately, TeraWulf has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its 50.1% ownership interest in the Abernathy Joint Venture to an investor group led by its joint venture partner, Fluidstack. The transaction monetizes TeraWulf's approximately $450 million investment at a premium to invested capital, unlocking significant capital for redeployment into wholly owned AI infrastructure opportunities. Collectively, the transactions enhance TeraWulf’s long-term revenue visibility, strengthen its financial position, and further align the Company’s capital with infrastructure platforms where it maintains direct ownership, customer relationships, and operational control. Anthropic Executes 20-Year Lease at Justified Data Campus TeraWulf has entered into a 20-year lease agreement with Anthropic for a purpose-built AI infrastructure campus at the Justified Data site in Hawesville, Kentucky. The campus will accommodate approximately 401 MW of critical IT load and will be developed in multiple phases. Initial capacity is expected to be placed into service during the second half of 2027, with the campus ramping to the full 401 MW by early 2028. The lease is expected to generate approximately $19 billion of contracted lease revenue over the initial term and is expected to be supported by an investment-grade credit. TeraWulf Monetizes Abernathy Investment Under the terms of the Abernathy transaction, TeraWulf will sell its entire 50.1% ownership interest in the Abernathy Joint Venture to an investor group led by Fluidstack, its joint venture partner and a leading AI cloud infrastructure provider. The Abernathy Joint Venture was established in 2025 to develop a 168 MW critical IT load AI data center campus in Abernathy, Texas. Since the project's inception, TeraWulf and Fluidstack have worked closely to advance the development of the campus. Following the closing of the transaction, Fluidstack will continue to leading the project. The sale enables TeraWulf to realize the value created through its $450 million investment and redeploy that capital into AI infrastructure opportunities where it can capture greater long-term economic value through direct ownership and operation. Management Commentary Paul Prager, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of TeraWulf, commented: “When we announced the Justified Data campus acquisition in February, we told investors that we expected to secure a major customer commitment by around the end of the second quarter of 2026. The timing of today's announcement reflects the completion of final documentation and customary transaction processes, and we are proud to announce this landmark partnership with Anthropic.” “The Anthropic lease validates our strategy and establishes a long-duration revenue stream with one of the world’s leading AI companies. The lease provides approximately $19 billion of contracted lease revenue over its initial term, creates a framework for future expansion, and demonstrates the value of our ability to source power, develop infrastructure, and secure long-term customer commitments.” “At the same time, the sale of our ownership interest in Abernathy to a group led by Fluidstack crystallizes the value created through that investment and generates significant capital for redeployment into infrastructure platforms where we maintain direct ownership, customer relationships, and operational control.” “Together, these transactions position TeraWulf for its next phase of growth. Our strategy is centered on owning and operating critical infrastructure assets, maintaining direct relationships with our customers, and controlling the long-term evolution of our campuses. We believe this model provides the greatest opportunity to generate durable cash flows and attractive long-term returns for shareholders.” Strategic Benefits Following completion of the transactions, TeraWulf expects to: Add approximately $19 billion of contracted revenue under the initial 20-year lease term. Further expand its long-term infrastructure relationship with Anthropic, one of the world's leading AI companies. Bring the initial Anthropic capacity at Justified Data online in the second half of 2027. Monetize its approximately $450 million investment in the Abernathy Joint Venture at a premium to invested capital, while simplifying TeraWulf's financial statements and streamlining financial reporting through the elimination of joint venture accounting. Recycle capital into wholly owned AI infrastructure opportunities where TeraWulf can capture greater long-term economic value through direct ownership and operation. Further strengthen TeraWulf’s position as a leading owner, developer, and operator of AI infrastructure. Together, these transactions demonstrate TeraWulf's ability to create value across the AI infrastructure lifecycle – from originating and developing large-scale campuses, to securing long-term customer commitments, to monetizing mature infrastructure investments and redeploying capital into future growth opportunities. About TeraWulf TeraWulf develops, owns, and operates large-scale digital infrastructure designed to support AI, high-performance computing (HPC), and other advanced compute workloads. Leveraging deep expertise in energy markets, power infrastructure, and grid integration, the Company develops and operates purpose-built facilities where power availability, scalability, and operational execution are critical competitive advantages. By strategically securing and monetizing high-value power resources, TeraWulf is well-positioned to serve the growing infrastructure needs of hyperscalers, AI innovators, and enterprise customers. Learn more at terawulf.com . title: Sleep Calculator
summary: Prepping for an early wakeup? Never seem to feel rested? Discover your recommended sleep/wake time with the sleep calculator.
body_text: Sleep Calculator Cycles (Quick Answer) To wake up refreshed, go to bed in 90-minute cycles: 5 cycles = 7.5 hours (ideal) 6 cycles = 9 hours (optimal) Example: Wake at 6:00 AM → Sleep at: 9:00 PM (9 hours) 10:30 PM (7.5 hours) 💡 Tip: Falling asleep takes ~15 minutes, so adjust accordingly. Why are Sleep or Bedtime Calculators Helpful? Struggling to wake up feeling rested? You’re not alone. Many people search for a sleep calculator or bedtime calculation tool to find their “perfect” bedtime based on sleep cycles. But most calculators stop there. They don’t consider what really affects sleep: your habits, stress, unique internal rhythms, and the disconnect between your brain and body that often causes sleep issues. The consequences of poor sleep can affect many aspects of daily life , leading to impaired mental performance and feeling tired and moody. Many people often ask: Is 10pm to 4am enough sleep? Is 11pm to 5am enough sleep? What time should I go to bed if I wake up at 5am? When should I wake up to optimize my sleep cycle? Dr. Michael Grandner, Sleep Expert, Professor of Neuroscience and Physiological Sciences: “Understanding your personal circadian rhythm is more effective than rigidly sticking to one set schedule.” We go beyond simple timing. Your sleep time calculator result is a starting point, not a standalone solution. We help you understand why knowing your ideal bedtime isn't enough to actually fall asleep faster, stay asleep longer, and wake up refreshed. We connect this timing with science-backed strategies to help you truly optimize your sleep quality, not just your sleep quantity. Wake Up Refreshed—Start With the Right Sleep Calculator with REM Use our free sleep cycle calculator below to find your ideal bedtime or wake-up time, based on natural 90-minute sleep cycles. Then, discover why timing is only one piece of the puzzle, and how proven CBT-I sleep strategies can help you bridge the gap between knowing your ideal bedtime and actually achieving restful sleep. Dr. Areti Vassilopoulos, PsyD — Clinical Psychologist & Sleep Specialist You can't just 'catch up' on sleep. Using a sleep calculator can help you be intentional about your sleep schedule and build a healthier, more consistent routine. How the Sleep Cycle Calculator Works - Best Time To Sleep and Wake Up Here’s the math behind better mornings: Each sleep cycle = ~90 minutes 5 full sleep cycles = ~7.5 hours Count backwards 7.5 hours from your wake-up time to find your optimal bedtime Example: Wake-up time: 6:00 a.m. → Bedtime: 10:30 p.m. Try this bedtime for a week. The goal is to wake naturally 5–10 minutes before your alarm. Still waking with the alarm? Move bedtime earlier by 15 minutes. Waking too early? Shift it later. Try Our Popular Sleep Calculator Sleep Calculator Sleep Calculator Age Range 0-3 Months 4-11 Months 1-2 Years 3-5 Years 6-13 Years 14-17 Years 18-25 Years 26-35 Years 36-45 Years 46-55 Years 56-64 Years 65+ Years Sleep Schedule I want to wake up at... I want to go to bed at... : : Results It typically takes 15 minutes to fall asleep. If you're 26-35 years old and want to wake up refreshed at 8:00 AM , you should go to bed at one of the following times: ‍ Dr. Rachel Reiss, MD, Sleep Expert for Women: Knowing your ideal bedtime based on your wake-up time is one of the simplest yet most powerful ways to align your body with its natural circadian rhythm. A good night's sleep really does start with good timing. What Your Result Means (And What It Doesn’t) Dr. Daniel Jin Blum, Sleep Expert, Clinical Psychologist, Research Assistant Professor of Psychology “Tools like sleep calculators can help people understand their ideal bedtime based on wake time—but they’re just a starting point.” Our ideal bedtime calculator uses your input to align your bedtime with complete sleep cycles, each approximately 90 minutes long. This approach aims to help you wake up during a lighter stage of sleep, rather than disrupting deep sleep or REM sleep , which can reduce grogginess and improve how you feel upon waking. But here’s the crucial point: Even the perfect bedtime can’t fix underlying sleep disorders or poor sleep quality. If you’re lying awake at 2 a.m., waking repeatedly throughout the night, or dragging through the day despite getting “enough” sleep hours, bedtime math alone won’t help. This can cause health problems that can be more severe . Knowing when to go to bed is one thing; being able to fall asleep and stay asleep is another. Sleep Efficiency & Sleep Cycles Explained: Are You Really Sleeping Well? Use this simple formula to estimate your sleep quality: Sleep Efficiency Diagram How Actual Sleep Time is Calculated Total time in bed − Time to fall asleep − Minutes awake during night = Actual sleep time In bed: 7 hours (420 min) Time to fall asleep: 25 min Awake during night: 25 min Actual sleep: 370 min Sleep Efficiency Formula Sleep Efficiency = Actual sleep time ÷ Total time in bed × 100% Sleep efficiency = 370 ÷ 420 = 88% ✅ 💡 Healthy target: 85% or higher ‍ Why Sleep Quality Matters (Not Just Sleep Hours) Eight hours of fragmented, poor-quality sleep isn’t better than six hours of solid, uninterrupted rest. Improving your sleep hygiene—from limiting screens before bed to managing stress effectively—is key to achieving restorative sleep. Regular exercise may improve your sleep quality. You need to learn how to actively improve your sleep quality, addressing the root causes of your sleep issues, rather than just tracking your hours. We empower you with strategies to build a reliable bedtime routine and truly rest. You can also discover 5 effective ways to improve your sleep and explore sleep compression as a technique for improving sleep quality . How Much Sleep Do You Really Need? Recommended Sleep by Age Age Group Recommended Sleep 4–12 months 12–16 hrs 1–2 years 11–14 hrs 3–5 years 10–13 hrs 6–12 years 9–12 hrs 13–18 years 8–10 hrs 18+ years 7+ hrs ‍ But hours alone don’t tell the whole story. Quality and timing matter, too. An average adult goes through several sleep cycles each night, with each cycle lasting about 90 to 120 minutes. To feel your best, aim for at least four complete sleep cycles. For a more precise recommendation, consider using a sleep calculator that factors in your age and bedtime. ‍ How Sleep Works: Cycles, Stages, and Timing Sleep is crucial for nearly every bodily system. Getting enough sleep allows your mind and body to benefit from its restorative effects and helps you avoid the negative consequences of sleep deprivation. Sleep isn’t just one long rest—it’s a series of intricate sleep cycles, each with distinct stages of sleep. Typically, you cycle through all four stages multiple times each night. The first three stages are known as non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep: Stages 1 and 2 are lighter sleep phases where your body and mind begin to relax and slow down. Stage 3 is deep sleep, considered essential for both physical and mental recovery. The fourth stage is rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. During this stage, most of your body is temporarily paralyzed, but brain activity significantly increases, and your eyes move rapidly behind your closed eyelids. This is when the most intense dreaming occurs, which is vital for memory and complex thinking when you're awake. Early in the night, you spend more time in NREM sleep, while later cycles feature more REM sleep. Researchers believe this combination of NREM and REM sleep throughout the night is what allows you to wake up feeling physically and mentally refreshed. When you don't get enough sleep, you disrupt these cycles, preventing you from getting the necessary balance of NREM and REM sleep, which can have significant repercussions for your overall health and well-being. Deep sleep is crucial for physical restoration and growth, while REM sleep supports memory consolidation and memory and mood regulation . Waking mid-cycle, especially during deep sleep, can leave you feeling groggy and disoriented, even if you’ve spent how many hours of sleep in bed. That’s why aligning your bedtime with your natural cycles, as a sleep cycle calculator suggests, matters—but it's just one piece of the puzzle. ‍ Finding Your Ideal Sleep Schedule Your best bedtime truly depends on your individual biology and lifestyle. Some people are natural night owls, while others are early birds. Factors like shift work, parenthood, or even jet lag can significantly impact your circadian rhythm. Many also find themselves needing to "catch up" on sleep on weekends . While a sleep time calculator is a great starting point, flexible, evidence-based support is what makes the real difference in establishing a sustainable, healthy bedtime routine that works for you . Dr. Shiyan Yeo, MD Sleep calculators are useful starting points. When you match your sleep timing with your biology, you improve not just sleep — but mood, energy, and even immune health. Use this sleep calculator table to find the best bedtime based on your wake-up time. Is Your Sleep Good Enough? Ask yourself: Do you wake up tired or groggy? Do you struggle to fall asleep or stay asleep? Do you need naps or caffeine to get through the day? If yes, it’s time to go beyond bedtime math. Why Most Sleep Advice Doesn’t Work You’ve probably tried a lot—cutting back on screens, drinking sleepytime tea, sticking to a strict bedtime. These tips might help a little, but they don’t solve the real problem. Most sleep advice focuses only on surface-level habits. But if your brain and body are stuck in a cycle of poor sleep, stress, and frustration, no amount of lavender oil or early alarms will fix it. The truth is, sleep issues are often driven by how you think about sleep, your emotional responses to restlessness, and patterns that have become wired into your daily routine. That’s why lasting improvement requires more than a checklist—it takes a deeper approach. Tailored Strategies for Better Sleep Sleep Reset combines the insights from your ideal bedtime calculator result with proven behavioral interventions drawn from CBT-I. We teach you to: Strengthen your bedtime routine and create a positive sleep environment. Address the root causes of your sleep issues, including sleep-related anxiety. Rebuild your body’s natural trust in its sleep rhythm. Learn how to get better sleep without pills through sustainable habit changes and explore naturally remedies for sleep . Looking for more than a quick calculation? Join the tends of thousands who’ve discovered that the secret to better sleep isn’t just when you go to bed—it’s how you live before, during, and after. Why CBT-I Is the Gold Standard for Better Sleep Most people struggling with sleep deprivation and deficiency or chronic sleep issues don’t need medication—they need the right habits and mindset. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) is the clinical gold standard for treating sleep problems, with decades of scientific proof. According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH) , it’s a drug-free, evidence-based approach that addresses the root causes of sleep difficulties. Sleep Reset’s program uses CBT-I principles to help you: Break the cycle of anxiety and depression around sleep, a common benefit of techniques like sleep compression . Rebuild a reliable bedtime routine. Address issues like circadian rhythm misalignment and persistent sleep difficulties. Improve both sleep quality vs sleep quantity. CBT-I isn’t about willpower—it’s about science. Research by Dr. James B. Maas at the American Psychological Association (APA) and the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) confirms its efficacy. And Sleep Reset brings it to your phone, without pills or side effects, making it easier than ever to learn how to get better sleep without pills . If you're fighting insomnia with CBT for insomnia , you'll find our approach invaluable Standard Sleep Calculators vs. Sleep Reset Feature Standard Sleep Calculator Sleep Reset Calculates ideal bedtime ✓ ✓ Based on sleep cycles ✓ ✓ Personalizes advice ✗ ✓ Tailored to your unique sleep challenges Considers habits, stress, rhythm ✗ ✓ Integrates these into your personalized plan Offers proven CBT-I strategies ✗ ✓ Foundation of our program Helps fix actual sleep issues ✗ ✓ Addresses root causes of poor sleep Real Results From Real Sleep Reset Members "I used to dread bedtime because I knew I wouldn't fall asleep. With Sleep Reset, I fall asleep faster and wake up feeling human again." —Maya, 37 "The sleep calculator was a helpful start, but the real change came from fixing my bedtime routine and stress habits. I'm finally sleeping through the night." —Josh, 44 "I used to think how many hours of sleep was enough. Now I know it’s not just about hours—it’s about cycles and quality. Sleep Reset changed everything." —Lauren, 29 Ready to Go Beyond a Bedtime Guess? You’ve got your result from the sleep time calculator—now make it count. Sleep Reset helps you turn bedtime into real, restful sleep by addressing the underlying reasons you might be struggling. Read more about CBTI - the gold standard for getting a good night's sleep! Start your free sleep quiz to get a personalized sleep plan rooted in CBT-I! Start your sleep quiz Sleep Calculator Questions People Also Ask What Is a Sleep Calculator? A sleep calculator is a tool that determines the best time to fall asleep or wake up based on 90-minute sleep cycles. It helps you wake up between cycles instead of during deep sleep, reducing grogginess. Is 10 PM to 4 AM enough sleep? No. That’s only 6 hours (4 cycles). Most adults need 7–9 hours. What time should I sleep if I wake at 5 AM? Try: 9:30 PM (7.5 hours) 8:00 PM (9 hours) How do sleep cycles work? Each cycle lasts ~90 minutes. Waking between cycles reduces grogginess. Is 6 hours of sleep enough? Only for a small percentage of people. Most need at least 7 hours. How many sleep cycles do you need per night? Most adults need 4–6 sleep cycles per night. Each cycle lasts about 90 minutes, so this equals 6 to 9 hours of sleep. How long does it take to fall asleep? On average, it takes 10–20 minutes to fall asleep. When using a sleep calculator, you should factor this in. What happens if you wake up in the middle of a sleep cycle? Waking during deep sleep can make you feel groggy and disoriented, a phenomenon known as sleep inertia. Is it better to wake up after 6 hours or 7 hours? 6 hours aligns with 4 sleep cycles, while 7 hours interrupts a cycle. In many cases, 6 hours may feel better than 7—but 7.5 hours is ideal. What time should I go to bed if I wake up at 4 AM? Try: 8:30 PM (7.5 hours) 7:00 PM (9 hours) What time should I sleep if I wake up at 6 AM? Try: 10:30 PM (7.5 hours) 9:00 PM (9 hours) What is the best bedtime for waking up early? The best bedtime depends on completing full 90-minute cycles. For most people, this means going to bed between 9 PM and 11 PM. Can I train my body to wake up without an alarm? Yes. By maintaining a consistent sleep schedule aligned with your circadian rhythm, your body can naturally wake up without an alarm. Why do I still feel tired after 8 hours of sleep? Poor sleep quality, frequent awakenings, or misaligned sleep cycles can leave you feeling tired even after enough hours. What is sleep inertia? Sleep inertia is the groggy feeling you experience when waking up from deep sleep. It can last from a few minutes to over an hour. Does napping affect sleep cycles? Yes. Long or late naps can disrupt your nighttime sleep cycles and make it harder to fall asleep. How do I fix a broken sleep schedule? Gradually shift your bedtime by 15–30 minutes each night and maintain consistent wake-up times, even on weekends. What is REM sleep and why does it matter? REM sleep is the stage where dreaming occurs and is essential for memory, learning, and emotional regulation. What is deep sleep? Deep sleep is the most restorative stage of sleep, crucial for physical recovery and immune function. What is a circadian rhythm? Your circadian rhythm is your body’s internal clock that regulates sleep and wake cycles over a 24-hour period. Can you catch up on sleep? You can recover some sleep debt, but inconsistent sleep patterns can still negatively affect your health.

body_text: At TTM Technologies, we're proud to highlight a milestone that reflects our commitment to pushing the boundaries of advanced interconnect solutions: the development and delivery of Asymmetric Printed Circuit Board (“PCB”) N+M Technology. Achievements like this are what cement our position as the leader in AI interconnect solutions. What is Asymmetric PCB N+M Technology? Modern electronics are pushing the limits of what printed circuit boards can do. As devices become faster and more powerful, managing how signals travel and how power is distributed across a board becomes increasingly complex – and increasingly critical. N+M technology is TTM's answer to that challenge. Built on a hybrid asymmetric architecture — a design approach that separates the board into distinct sections, N+M dedicates separate PCB sub-sections to high-speed data transmission and power management in different thickness, respectively. By keeping these functions separate, N+M minimizes interference and allows each to perform at its greatest potential. Drilling Room in TTM Facility The result is a cleaner, more reliable signal and more efficient power performance — two things that matter enormously in today's high-demand electronics applications. The Challenge We Set Out to Solve The rapid growth of AI infrastructure, data centers, and advanced networking has created new and complex demands on printed circuit board technology. Customers in these spaces require solutions that deliver exceptional signal integrity and power performance catering different cable sizes – without compromising on quality, reliability, or manufacturability. TTM recognized this need early and took early development with the customers and decisive action. How TTM Delivered Bringing N+M technology to market required more than technical expertise; it demanded a coordinated, strategic effort across our organization. Our dedicated N+M Task Force was assembled to do exactly that. Asymmetric PCB The team focused on four key areas: Clear Timelines: Establishing and meeting defined timelines to ensure customers could plan and execute with confidence Drive Development Builds: Rigorously proving out the technology's capabilities before bringing it to market Capital Investment: Making the right infrastructure and capacity investments to support long-term customer needs Design Guidance: Delivering fully documented customer design guidelines to improve product quality, reliability, and performance — and to ensure seamless customer adoption The result was a technology solution that was not only technically groundbreaking but also ready for real-world, large-scale deployment. TTM's Position as the Advanced Technology Partner of Choice The successful delivery of N+M technology reinforces what our customers already know — TTM is more than a printed circuit board manufacturer. We are a strategic technology partner, committed to staying at the cutting edge of advanced interconnect technology. This milestone also reflects our broader strategy of aligning with the megatrends shaping the electronics industry — from AI, hyperscale data centers, and networking to aerospace, defense, and beyond. By investing in technologies like N+M, we are ensuring that TTM remains at the forefront of innovation for years to come. Looking Ahead The development of N+M technology is just one example of TTM's continued investment in the future. As customer needs evolve and the pace of technological change accelerates, we remain committed to delivering the advanced solutions that keep our customers ahead of the curve.
